newsitem.title: BELGIUM: U.S. postpones action on anti-EU meat sanctions.
newsitem.headline: U.S. postpones action on anti-EU meat sanctions.

text.p: The United States has postponed to April 30 threatened action against EU meat imports to allow transatlantic talks on veterinary standards to continue, a European Commission spokesman said on Tuesday.
The move came as Washington faced a self-imposed deadline for a deal to be reached with Brussels to end a three-year dispute.
Washington had said that if no deal was reached by Tuesday it would remove more than 100 European meat and poultry plants from its approved exporters list.
Such an action could halt up to $300 million worth of EU meat shipments to the United States, mostly pork products from Denmark and ham from Italy.
"The Americans have called off any action until April 30 to allow talks to continue," the spokesman told Reuters.
At issue in the dispute are veterinary inspections of imported animal products.
On April 1, the 15-nation EU introduced new rules which U.S. officials say block about $100 million-worth of U.S. exports to Europe.

The new rules were introduced after the failure of the two sides to reach agreement in talks which began after the end of the Uruguay Round of negotiations under the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade three years ago.
A U.S. Agriculture Department officials said on Monday that EU negotiatiors would head back to Washington for talks on Wednesday.

EU officials said on Monday that agreement was close between the two sides expect over poultry imports. The 15-nation bloc was expecting to hear from the U.S. about whether a deal could be reached that excluded poultry for now.
The complicated talks have covered a wide range of issues and sectors -- including the beef and pork industry, the poultry industry, the pet food sector, and the dairy and egg sectors.
